label: the weight is a signed count
why: `push $0; push %eax; fildll` is the zero-extending conversion GCC uses for `unsigned int`; a signed count would have been a bare `fildl`.  The two agree on every total below 2^31, which is why the fixture starts three of its runs near the boundary and asserts it crossed.

label: the new sample carries a weight of one
the first-call test is on the average, not on the count
the first call averages rather than assigns
the running average rounds at every step
why: PROVEN, not assumed.  The two forms were compiled with this tree's own CXXFLAGS and `objdump -d` diffed over `_ZN22V90ConnectionEvaluator14updateAvePdsnrEfj`: the instruction text is IDENTICAL, operands included.  The reason is the one CLAUDE.md gives for not using -ffloat-store -- a `float` LOCAL is not a rounding point, because GCC keeps it in an x87 register at 80-bit extended and rounds only where a value reaches memory.  Both forms round exactly once, at the `fstps` into +0x70.  So this is a mutation that cannot fail, and the interesting part is that the obvious reading of it -- 'three roundings instead of one' -- is wrong: naming a temporary does not create a rounding point on this target.  Assign it to a MEMBER instead of a local and it becomes a real defect.

label: the +0x9c store is 32 bits wide
why: 0x3e40e is `66 89 8b 9c 00 00 00` -- `mov %cx,0x9c(%ebx)`, a 16-bit store, so the object writes two bytes and this writes four. EQUIVALENT ONLY BECAUSE OF THAT ORDER: move the +0x9e store above the +0x9c one, or make anything between them read +0x9e, and this mutation becomes a real defect. It will then be CAUGHT and reported MIScounted, which is the point of registering it.
